_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Maintenance and Overhaul (M&O) Planning Documentation
summary: The M&O planning submission documents the contractor's overall plan for performing an item's overhaul in compliance with airworthiness and DMWR requirements, serving as a record of repairs and quality audits.
use_relationship:
The M&O planning submission provides fully documented processes to be performed during an item's overhaul. The M&O plan identifies the contractor's overall plan necessary to achieve an effective and efficient program to comply with airworthiness requirements within the Depot Maintenance Work Requirement (DMWR) or applicable M&O technical requirements. The plan serves as a record of repairs performed and a system of records for quality audit purposes.
This Data Item Description (DID) contains format and content preparation instructions for the data product generated by the specific and discrete task requirement as delineated in the contract.
distribution_statement: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

preparation_instructions.title: Reference documents.
preparation_instructions.content: The applicable issue of the documents cited herein, including their approval dates and dates of any applicable amendments, notices, and revisions, shall be as specified in the contract.

children.title: The following items shall be identified on the cover page:
Company name, address, and Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code.
Part Number (PN) and National Stock Number (NSN) of the part being overhauled/repaired.
Plan revision level and revision date.
Reference the Depot Maintenance Work Requirement (DMWR) and release date or applicable M&O requirement.
All Maintenance Engineering Orders (MEOs) associated with the DMWR.
The following elements, at a minimum, shall be included on the remaining pages and reference the applicable DMWR paragraph or work package and MEOs in the operations in which they apply:
Receiving inspection instructions.
Disassembly instructions.
Cleaning instructions.
Overhaul Inspection Procedures.
Repair and replacement instructions.
Modification instructions (if applicable).
Reassembly instructions.
Testing instructions (if applicable).
Final assembly instructions.
Packaging instructions.
Additional requirements that shall be included:
All special tooling and test equipment shall be identified in each step where it is utilized.

When subcontractors are to be used for outsourced processes such as shot peen, metal plating, or non-destructive testing, the subcontractor's name, address, and CAGE code shall be provided at each applicable step in the plan.
children.content: Receiving inspection processes for operations performed by subcontractors shall be provided to ensure the parts are properly repaired/processed and all Certificates of Conformance (CoC) are complete.

children.title: The order of operations within the plan shall flow in the same sequence as the flow of operations in the facility.
Industry-recognized level III certification for Non-Destructive Testing (NDT).
Any deviations from prescribed operations or procedures that the DMWR requires shall be provided with substantiation.
Required additional documentation:
Master Tooling Certification:
children.content: Include a written statement certifying possession of or access to any special tooling, inspection, or test equipment required by the latest DMWR revision. If equivalent tooling is utilized in lieu of the required tooling from the DMWR, include a complete technical description of the tooling with sufficient substantiation to determine an equivalency, i.e., form, fit, and function. Identify the availability of the DMWR-specified test equipment or if equivalent test equipment has been procured or built "in-house."

children.title: A list of all proposed subcontractors that will be used to perform M&O processes and a copy of the M&O plan or processes that the Government deems significant to the overhaul regardless of the criticality of the process/procedure.
children.content: Please refer to Table 1-1 below as examples of processes that are always considered significant.

children.title: Critical Safety Item (CSI) Requirements.
children.content: For contracts that provide overhaul services for Army Aviation CSIs, the M&O plan shall adhere to AMCOM Regulation 702-7, Aviation Critical Safety Items, Critical Application Items, and New Source Testing Program Management, 19 June 2017, Appendix D, Quality Engineering Standard-2 (QE-STD-2), Revision C. As integrated within the M&O planning submission, contractors shall demonstrate an understanding of the sequence of processes and the controls required to maintain the integrity of the Critical Characteristics (CCs) for the processes performed by both the contractor applicant and its proposed subcontractors. Highlights from QE-STD-2 of M&O planning additional submission requirements for CSIs are as follows:

children.title: Each page of the plan and any proposed subcontractor planning that affects a CC shall contain a statement such as "This item is a Critical Safety Item (CSI)" and shall reference QE-STD-2.
Detailed subcontractor process plans must be provided for any outsourced process that impacts or involves a CC.
Plans required for CCs include but are not limited to, Non-Destructive Inspection/Testing and Metal Plating. Shot Peen plans are required for all parts, regardless of criticality.
Clear identification within the plan of all CCs is required in a manner that draws attention. Any method utilized for this identification is acceptable, e.g., <<CC>>, **CC**, etc.
A statement shall be included that the contractor will conduct a required 100% inspection of all CCs prior to moving to subsequent operations.
All CCs in the plan shall be written to provide adequate space for a Quality Inspector to verify completion of the applicable step.
When a measurement is taken for any CC operation
children.content: or any other DMWR-required inspection (e.g., dimension, torque, surface finish, voltage, etc.), the characteristic inspection, actual measurement, date of inspection, identity of mechanic and quality inspector, calibrated tooling (name or serial number), and calibration due date must be documented in the CC step. If the company has a master sheet with the Test, Measurement, and Diagnostic Equipment (TMDE) information, the tool reference number may be documented in that operation. Measurement equipment shall conform to the accuracy requirements specified in QE-STD-2.

children.title: A separate document shall be provided that addresses how the requirements of QE-STD-2 will be complied with.
children.content: This requirement can normally be met by modifying and providing the company's current quality plan to incorporate the QE-STD-2 requirements.

children.title: If overhaul requires the procurement of CSI sub-components or repair parts, these parts shall adhere to Appendix C of AMCOM Regulation 702-7, Quality Engineering Standard-1 (QE-STD-1), Revision E.
children.content: The M&O plan shall address how the requirements of QE-STD-1 will be complied with.
